name: Prototyping

claims.claim_text: DIP-packaged microcontrollers survive because prototyping needs them: a through-hole part can be pulled and replaced in seconds when a static discharge kills it, which is not true of a soldered SMD device.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's a winter day and you're wearing wool socks and you walk over to your launch pad and you zap it, you need to just switch it out real quick
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Designing a switching DC-DC converter from scratch rather than using an off-the-shelf regulator adds a prototyping cycle, which is one reason cost-sensitive designs step voltages up or down with standard parts instead.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you've got to design a DC to DC converter, geez, you might have to prototype that
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Cores, Digikey, Electronic Design - The Commercial Competitor Commencement

claims.claim_text: Silicon vendors have continued to release modern cores in through-hole packages aimed at breadboard work; NXP introduced a Cortex-M0 in a DIP package, a package choice justified by prototyping rather than by volume production.
claims.quote_verbatim: they put a Cortex M zero in a dip package
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Radiation Chips & Old Package Types - Technocratic Toilet Troubleshooting

claims.claim_text: Desktop 3D printing is used for enclosure and packaging prototypes rather than volume parts, on the reasoning that a printed case need only be functional, not cosmetically finished, at the proto stage.
claims.quote_verbatim: if it doesn't need to look super pretty and you could print it on your desk, I mean, it wouldn't be a volume situation, but you could at least prototype
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A crowdfunded hardware program can be launched from an early proof of concept plus a user-interface mock-up and a render of a pre-beta board, with the design then carried through a production run of a couple of hundred units.
claims.quote_verbatim: started the Kickstarter with an early proof of concept and a UI mock-up and a render of our pre-beta board and taking it all the way through a couple hundred unit production run
claims.speaker: Ian Danaher
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ian Daniher - Nascent Nonolith Numquid

claims.claim_text: A consulting practice can be protected by prototyping the single riskiest sub-block of a proposed job before accepting it, so that an unsolvable problem is discovered during the quote rather than after the contract is signed.
claims.quote_verbatim: I will occasionally say, look, you know, I think I can do this, but I'm going to go away, like prototype some little bit of it.
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Mike Harrison - X-ray Examining Xenogogue

claims.claim_text: A concept demonstration built in a day proves only a limited case; expanding that demonstration into something that works in every case is typically a further twenty or so iterations.
claims.quote_verbatim: Oh, well, that's 20 different iterations.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: FPGAs, Robots & Thermocouples - Wampum's Wavering Worth

claims.claim_text: Front-page datasheet features can hide tolerances that break a design idea: a chip advertised with built-in current limiting may specify 15 percent tolerance on that limit over temperature, which rules out using it as a precision current source.
claims.quote_verbatim: tolerance of 15% on the current limit
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Arduino, IndiGoGo and Hack-a-Day - Doodad Dealer Dancing

claims.claim_text: The recommended sequence for evaluating a promising part is to read the full datasheet including the footnoted tolerances first, and then build a prototype to confirm the behaviour before designing around it.
claims.quote_verbatim: Read your data sheets and then prototype, folks.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Arduino, IndiGoGo and Hack-a-Day - Doodad Dealer Dancing

claims.claim_text: In-house forming and machining cannot match the throughput of a large stamping press and are therefore used only for prototype parts, not production runs.
claims.quote_verbatim: This is for prototyping only.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Tesla, FPGAs and DigiKey - Zesty Zippy Zynq

claims.claim_text: Keeping prototype fabrication in-house shortens the loop mainly by removing the outbound shipment and the retooling penalty, so a mistake costs another in-house run rather than a new tool and a new lead time.
claims.quote_verbatim: the prototyping is so much faster just because you don't have to send it out
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Tesla, FPGAs and DigiKey - Zesty Zippy Zynq

claims.claim_text: A twelve-week component lead time desynchronises prototyping from procurement: by the time the ordered part arrives and is fitted and tested, the board may already be three or four revisions further on, leaving several live versions of the design to track.
claims.quote_verbatim: you get a 12-week lead time of part. By the time this part shows up, and you get it into a unit, and you get it tested, you've already got three or four more revs of the board done already
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Funding New/Manufacturing Old Projects - Radical Robotic Requisition

claims.claim_text: A nominally locked-down hardware design still accumulates prototype changes, because engineers keep trying new variants and correcting mistakes after the freeze.
claims.quote_verbatim: You're still going to be prototyping new things, even when you have a quote-unquote lockdown design.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Funding New/Manufacturing Old Projects - Radical Robotic Requisition

claims.claim_text: Even after a production panel has been ordered and passes quality inspection, small mechanical corrections keep surfacing, such as enlarging a hole by 0.2 mm because a connector lacks margin and a switch wobbles, or nudging silkscreen a couple of millimetres.
claims.quote_verbatim: I'd like that hole 0.2 millimeters bigger, because maybe there's not enough margin in the connector, and that switch wobbles just a little bit.
claims.episode_title: Funding New/Manufacturing Old Projects - Radical Robotic Requisition

claims.claim_text: During safety and EMC compliance testing, a design change costs no extra test fee but pauses the certification schedule until a corrected unit is delivered, which makes the change expensive in calendar time.
claims.quote_verbatim: anytime that they find a need for a design change, uh, it is a schedule hit and it's an expensive schedule hit
claims.speaker: Eric Van Wyk
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Eric VanWyk - Meiotic Mountenance Mooshimeter

claims.claim_text: Compliance testing compresses the turn time a team is used to: a two-week prototype turn becomes a same-day emergency build, because the certification slot stays paused until the fixed board arrives.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're used to saying, oh, I can do this on a two week turn time
claims.speaker: Eric Van Wyk
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Eric VanWyk - Meiotic Mountenance Mooshimeter

claims.claim_text: A one-person consultancy can cover prototype-quantity parts from personal stock accumulated over thirty years, improvising or desoldering from an old board rather than ordering, because prototype quantities are small enough for that to work.
claims.quote_verbatim: For the sort of quantities I need for prototyping, you know, I've either got or I can improvise or I can pull on off of a board.
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Prototype stock stays usable if leftovers are filtered out of the project box back into general stock as soon as each project finishes, so the inventory remains searchable from memory.
claims.quote_verbatim: Generally, I'm quite good at filtering the leftovers out of the project box into general stock as soon as the project's finished.
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Prototype builds are often placed with domestic assembly houses purely for turnaround speed, with the move to lower-cost offshore manufacture deferred until quantities rise.
claims.quote_verbatim: Certainly a lot of the prototyping that I do is US-based manufacturing, just for the pure reason of speed.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: MightyHohm For The Holidays - Kaiser Keyzer's Kits

claims.claim_text: Functionality that does not exist yet can be faked by a human during a prototype demonstration, a Mechanical Turk approach exemplified by an engineer behind a trade-show booth manually switching an LED that the product is supposed to control.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're like at a trade show and you're the guy behind the booth, like flipping, flipping the LED
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Matt Richardson - Raspberry Risorgimento Regent

claims.claim_text: Manufacturability and prototypability are separate properties: a process can be viable in volume yet offer no way to make one-off samples, which blocks experimentation until someone brings the process down to prototype scale.
claims.quote_verbatim: even if something is manufacturable. It's not necessarily prototypable.
claims.speaker: Ariel Briner
claims.episode_title: An interview with Ariel Briner of Cartesian Co

claims.claim_text: Inkjet-style conductive printing onto fabric is difficult because the substrate is floppy rather than flat and must be stretched taut to hold a controlled distance between print head and material.
claims.quote_verbatim: because the fabric, like, is all floppy. It's not flat. You have to maybe stretch it to, you know, get it nice and tight.
claims.episode_title: An interview with Ariel Briner of Cartesian Co

claims.claim_text: For most one-off circuit experiments, dead-bug construction, Manhattan-style pads, or a hand-cut board are faster and cheaper routes than buying dedicated prototyping hardware.
claims.quote_verbatim: man, just dead bug it or, you know, cut a board or something. Manhattan style.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Front-end concept work on a small mechatronic build, covering sketches and a couple of schematics, can consume ten to twenty hours before any hardware is assembled.
claims.quote_verbatim: just doing some sketches, a couple of schematics that took easily like 10 to 20 hours
claims.speaker: Great Scott

claims.claim_text: Prototyping in an unfamiliar mechanical domain exposes constraints that cannot be predicted on paper; an enclosure sized to hold batteries and drivers can be found to obstruct movement only once the assembly is ridden or operated.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you try to prototype something, you don't have practical experience
claims.speaker: Great Scott

claims.claim_text: Interpreted environments such as Lua VMs and Python are used to churn out prototypes and proofs of concept quickly, with the design reimplemented more rigorously once the product will be built in more than about five units.
claims.quote_verbatim: it allows me to really quickly churn out prototypes and proof of concept and stuff but when when i for product that i am designing and ultimately will be producing more than five off i i would like to do it a bit more properly
claims.speaker: Omer Kilic

claims.claim_text: Prototyping deliberately trades unit economics for information: single-piece and low-quantity versions cost more per unit, and that premium buys knowledge of what is actually needed before committing to volume.
claims.quote_verbatim: You pay more up front for the single piece versions.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The same logic applies to capital equipment for a prototyping shop: using shared or outsourced services first establishes which machines are genuinely needed, whereas buying up front on assumption leaves advanced equipment unused.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's why you use that stuff first. To figure out if you actually need it.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A first board should use an integrated chip or a module rather than a discrete implementation, so the design gets finished and can then be revisited for cost optimisation, instead of never converging.
claims.quote_verbatim: put a module down or put a chip down and then go back and optimize it later for cost or whatever you can. But just get it done first and then revise it.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A convincing crowdfunding demonstration can be a purely cosmetic prototype, for example a cast acrylic model with no electronics, firmware, or software inside, which is why appearance-only prototypes are a poor proxy for engineering progress.
claims.quote_verbatim: There were no electronics inside. There were no, there was no firmware written.
claims.speaker: Josh Lifton

claims.claim_text: The governing priority in early prototyping is to get a working artifact in hand, accepting that the first version will be slow and rough, with refinement deferred to later passes.
claims.quote_verbatim: the most important thing is just to get a thing in hand and working. And then, yeah, it's going to be slow. It's going to be chunky at first.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Semiconductor vendors have shipped Arduino-form-factor shields for their analogue parts, letting a hardware engineer read and write device registers and pull a data stream out of an ADC without writing low-level firmware first.
claims.quote_verbatim: linear tech, they started developing Arduino shields for their parts
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Under a hard deadline such as a 24-hour hackathon, running interpreted code on an existing board displaces spinning a custom board and bringing it up bare metal, because only the former fits the time budget.
claims.quote_verbatim: Maybe if I wanted, I could spin my own board and like bring this whole thing up bare metal, but you know, we've got 24 hours.

claims.claim_text: Scripting-language embedded platforms are aimed at the fast-iteration prototype stage; a shipping product is usually handed to an embedded specialist to tighten up, unless the device is simple enough that no drop to low-level code is required.
claims.quote_verbatim: probably you would pay to send it to – bring an embedded person in and tighten that whole thing up
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Optical subsystems have been prototyped from salvage: laser diodes pulled out of old CD and DVD players supplied the emitters for early laser-scanning tracking experiments.
claims.quote_verbatim: they would just like grab like lasers off of like old CD players and DVD players rather. And like use that for prototyping
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A productive way to attack a concept that looks unworkable is to enumerate the specific reasons it should fail and then attempt each one, since many of the listed obstacles turn out to be individually solvable.
claims.quote_verbatim: we started looking at reasons why it wouldn't work. And then all of a sudden we realized that actually a lot of those reasons were solvable.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Effective prototypers suspend the demand for a finished-looking result and begin assembling immediately with expedient methods such as hot glue, treating the willingness to start as a learnable skill.
claims.quote_verbatim: just starting to hot glue and put things together
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Harvesting parts out of finished consumer products to build a prototype creates a trap: the demonstration works but the product cannot be built, because the salvaged item, such as an LCD, is only sold against a minimum order of panels.
claims.quote_verbatim: in prototyping, it's really tempting to steal parts from off the shelf products and make other products out of them
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: The realistic answer to how soon another prototype build can be made is the component lead time plus debug time, roughly twelve weeks plus however long it takes to bring up the batch of ten boards.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's like 12 weeks plus however long it takes us to debug those 10 boards
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Custom display suppliers rarely support prototype quantities from small unknown customers; the low-volume route that does exist, used for military LCDs, runs on the order of a thousand dollars per screen.
claims.quote_verbatim: how about a thousand dollars a screen?

claims.claim_text: When the objective is to get a prototype working quickly rather than to optimise it, C is a poor default and a higher-level embedded language such as MicroPython removes friction from the first pass.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're just trying to get stuff done, then C is not the way to go.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Deliberately constraining a prototyping session, for example by working at a remote cabin with only a hauled-in oscilloscope, soldering station and a fixed parts stock and no internet, forces completion with the resources on hand.
claims.quote_verbatim: I had a example where I constrained myself when I was prototyping. I think it's really important to do that.
claims.speaker: Zach Fredin

claims.claim_text: Small mechanical parts such as miniature planetary gear sets can be prototyped by machining a positive mould, casting a silicone negative from it, and then pouring urethane into the silicone, which yields multiple parts from one machining operation.
claims.quote_verbatim: he machines out this positive mold. And then he pours a negative mold with silicone. And then he pours urethane into that.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: 3D printing is properly classified as a prototyping tool rather than a manufacturing process, and most projects do not require owning the equipment: fabrication can be farmed out, and a Dremel and a file cover a large fraction of early mechanical work.
claims.quote_verbatim: You can get pretty far with a Dremel and a file too.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Lego Technic is expensive as a bulk prototyping material: priced by weight, 3D printer filament came out roughly seven to ten times cheaper per pound, with extruding filament from raw pellets offering about another factor of ten.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's like 10 X, seven X cheaper than Lego per pound or something like that
claims.speaker: Jason Huggins

claims.claim_text: A Lego Technic-compatible beam system, 8 mm wide with holes on 8 mm centres, supplies the fixed grid that makes early mechanical prototyping tractable, since a blank mechanical design offers no starting constraints.
claims.quote_verbatim: they're the same kind of dimensions as, as Lego techniques that are eight millimeters wide and the holes are eight millimeters center to center
claims.speaker: Jason Huggins

claims.claim_text: One mechanical design process starts by building physically from a bucket of standard parts on the desk and only afterwards designing the equivalent structure from scratch, removing the features the standard parts carried but the product does not need.
claims.quote_verbatim: I need a bucket, I need it like a box or a bucket of parts on my desk and I just start building. And then after the fact, I'll design it from scratch.
claims.speaker: Jason Huggins

claims.claim_text: Injection moulding is deferred while a product is still effectively in prototyping, because continual design updates would invalidate the tooling investment.
claims.quote_verbatim: why aren't you doing injection molding yet? And it's because you are still prototyping.

claims.claim_text: What distinguishes highly effective prototypers is tenacity and method rather than special equipment: they keep trying variations systematically instead of abandoning an approach at the first failure.
claims.quote_verbatim: the great prototyper, right. It's, it's, it's just tenacity.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Prototyping can be run as the scientific method: state a hypothesis about how the thing works, run a defined experiment against it, evaluate whether the hypothesis held, and cycle back with a revised hypothesis if it did not.
claims.quote_verbatim: I have a hypothesis and here's what it is. I'm going to try X, Y, Z and I try it. And then do I meet the hypothesis? If not, you know, cycle back through
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A common error is moving into PCB layout too early; bodging with existing hardware, wire-wrap, a dev board wired to a sensor breakout, or duct-taped assemblies answers the open questions before any board is committed.
claims.quote_verbatim: I would also caution though, as well, I jump into using PC, uh, layout programs way too fast.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Solderless breadboards and plug-in jumper wires are electrically adequate for prototyping up to roughly 10 MHz, above which parasitics of the interconnect start to matter.
claims.quote_verbatim: up until like about 10 megahertz or so, you don't really have to worry too much
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The first PCB CAD package a beginner learns tends to be the one they keep using for years, so the initial choice deserves more deliberation than it usually gets.
claims.quote_verbatim: whatever you pick as your first CAD program, you're probably getting used for a long time
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Hand prototyping is bounded by package technology: it stays feasible while parts remain hand-solderable, and BGA or fine-pitch TQFP devices push the work onto fabricated boards.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you're really good at prototyping and, and your parts are capable, if you're not using BGAs, if you're not using TQFPs or anything like that.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Owning enough machining capability to make basic prototype parts in-house pays off partly as a communication skill: the designer who has cut the part specifies it better and represents a more credible customer when the job is later sent to a machine shop.
claims.quote_verbatim: not only can I send it out, but you're so much smarter when you go to send it out because you know how the product needs to be designed
claims.speaker: John Saunders

claims.claim_text: A top-down prototyping approach starts from off-the-shelf modules such as a Feather-format board to prove the concept, since proving the concept is usually the hard part and custom hardware can follow.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's best to start with off the shelf modules, like a feather or something
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Waiting on fabricated boards stretches the time before a team learns whether an idea is viable at all, which is the main argument for using modules that are already in hand during the earliest spins.
claims.quote_verbatim: the longer you wait, the longer, the longer you stretch out your decision time of if it, if it's a viable idea
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Early prototypes benefit from off-the-shelf choices in power and mechanics: a coin cell is cheap and readily available as the initial power source, and a stock enclosure costs less and looks better than a 3D-printed case.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you could get like an off the shelf, uh, case as well to start with, that'll save you money
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Automated PCB design services have been offered as prototyping services at around $3,000 for a 24-hour turnaround, bounded by limits such as fewer than 50 components, 20 unique components, under 3 amps, under 500 MHz, and under 20 watts total.
claims.quote_verbatim: for $3,000 in 24 hours, they'll design your PCB as long as – I think they'll try to – a few other than 50 components, 20 unique components, less than 250 things, less than 3 amps, less than 500 megahertz, less than 20 watts total.
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Replacing breakout boards and plug-in prototype assemblies with a fabricated PCB removes the defining property of a prototype, which is that it can be changed easily; per-change fees make each iteration expensive rather than free.
claims.quote_verbatim: Completely missing that the entire point of a prototype is you can change it easily.
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Board fabrication lead time is not dead time in a prototype spin, because firmware can be written while the PCB is in fab, which is part of why compressing fab turnaround alone buys less than it appears.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you order your PCB from that, you can be writing the firmware while you're waiting for the PCB to get back
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Prototyping speed comes largely from keeping a standing library of known-good building blocks: a microcontroller always returned to, reusable code, and stock mechanical parts and subassemblies on the shelf.
claims.quote_verbatim: having a micro that you always go back to or having code that you go back to

claims.claim_text: A working mini electric motorbike was assembled in about three days entirely from parts already in the workshop, including eight-inch caster wheels, a spare motor and belt, T5 pulleys and a twist grip left over from an earlier project.
claims.quote_verbatim: I made it in about three days with CNC
claims.speaker: James Bruton

claims.claim_text: Corporate research labs use prototyping as a de-risking function: building and investigating a technology establishes whether a design path is worth pursuing, and the negative result is fed back to the business unit before product development money is spent.
claims.quote_verbatim: we essentially de-risk a particular technology before Nokia would take it over and product it
claims.speaker: Shahriar Shahramian

claims.claim_text: Integrated circuits built in such a research group are generally aimed at becoming a product in roughly four to five years, so the prototype horizon is far ahead of the current product line.
claims.quote_verbatim: targeted for potentially becoming a product in, let's say, four or five years or so
claims.speaker: Shahriar Shahramian

claims.claim_text: Modular, header-connected hardware such as an Arduino or Raspberry Pi is almost always the right choice for prototyping, because plugging known interfaces together is faster than fabricating an integrated board.
claims.quote_verbatim: from a prototyping perspective, it almost always makes sense to have some kind of modular thing
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The same modular construction is usually wrong for production, because connectors add cost, the stacked form factor is inefficient, and power consumption is not optimised for the application; the exception is a high-margin niche product where the module cost is immaterial.
claims.quote_verbatim: Adding, adding connectors adds, adds cost.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Prototypes built on general-purpose platforms do not scale: an installation demonstrated with about 200 LEDs behaves differently at 20,000, where power management fails first and data bandwidth second.
claims.quote_verbatim: we've baked these things with sort of 200 LEDs. Okay, this installation is just 20,000. And things, you know, things like power, you know, power management is the first thing and bandwidth and so on.
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison
claims.episode_title: LEDs and EVs with Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Customers who bring in a production-focused designer earlier, rather than after a prototype has been proven on hobbyist hardware, avoid re-engineering work because the scaling constraints are understood before the architecture is fixed.
claims.quote_verbatim: they are a lot better in getting me involved earlier
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison
claims.episode_title: LEDs and EVs with Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: The concrete engineering argument for moving prototype firmware to CircuitPython is measured iteration speed rather than platform preference.
claims.quote_verbatim: which is the prototyping is faster. I can tell you that specifically it is much faster.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Prototypes intended for user testing should represent what test participants expect the experience to be rather than a technically accurate simulation; in one case a hastily assembled mock built from televised race footage tested better than a physically accurate model.
claims.quote_verbatim: quickly waxed together a prototype that plays like a horse movie
claims.speaker: Zack Freedman

claims.claim_text: Engineers trained in prototyping-only organisations learn to design against functional requirements with cost as a secondary concern, a habit that has to be unlearned when moving to volume manufacturing.
claims.quote_verbatim: we were known to really, as a company that solved tough problems, but really just did prototyping
claims.speaker: Michael Corr
claims.episode_title: Product Lifecycle Management with Michael Corr

claims.claim_text: At volume the arithmetic of part selection changes sharply: saving ten cents of bill-of-materials cost across a million units returns one hundred thousand dollars, which is roughly the cost of another engineer.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're producing a million units and you can save 10 cents on your bill of materials
claims.speaker: Michael Corr
claims.episode_title: Product Lifecycle Management with Michael Corr

claims.claim_text: Prototype work performed for a prospective client is billable engineering time rather than a free sales activity, and treating it as free is a recognised failure mode of design consulting.
claims.quote_verbatim: you should prototype this for me for free
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: How much bring-up and debug infrastructure to break out on a module, such as the reset line, other debug pins, and individual per-module supplies allowing power sequencing, is a line drawn by application criticality rather than a universal rule; wire count and bundle thickness are the cost of that flexibility.
claims.quote_verbatim: do you implement individual power supplies for modules so that you can bring up and shut down, you know, sequence you can, should you go to the effort to power sequence stuff?
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Rigorous engineering stuff may be out the window

claims.claim_text: Off-the-shelf modules are designed for a prototype-then-respin workflow in which the module proves the concept and a custom board follows; using modules as quasi-production hardware leaves in compromises such as permanently enabled pull-ups.
claims.quote_verbatim: these are meant for like, you prototype with it and then, okay, you put it on your own board and then you're, you're good to go
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Rigorous engineering stuff may be out the window

claims.claim_text: XBee radios are convenient for prototyping because a pair configured through the vendor GUI behaves as a transparent point-to-point serial link, but their cost means designs are expected to move to another radio for volume.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's just like you put two XBs in between and it's like a serial terminal. It just pops out the other side.
claims.episode_title: Refrigerators and Robots with Amitabh Shrivastava

claims.claim_text: Low-power wide-area networks that work in a small prototype degrade as node count rises, because the available channels are few and slow and packet collisions increase, making network capacity, not link range, the limiting factor.
claims.quote_verbatim: as you have more devices in a network, you start to have more collisions
claims.episode_title: Refrigerators and Robots with Amitabh Shrivastava

claims.claim_text: A manufacturable product differs from the original dev-board prototype by essentially every measure, so the engineering effort of converting a proven prototype into a producible design is a distinct project rather than a cleanup pass.
claims.quote_verbatim: by the time you're in manufacturing, what you build is very different from that original Arduino prototype by almost every measure

claims.claim_text: For a build of only about three units, assembling a prototype from off-the-shelf components is cheaper and faster than a custom design, because custom engineering cost can only be amortised over a thousand or more units.
claims.quote_verbatim: Those three are going to be real expensive versus, you know, we can amortize my cost over a thousand, a couple thousand units.
claims.speaker: Andrea Longobardi
claims.episode_title: Low Power Connected Devices with Andrea Longobardi

claims.claim_text: Interaction design practice treats the prototype as the only reliable test of a design: build something people can actually operate, observe them using it, and iterate, because the quality of an interface is otherwise not knowable in advance.
claims.quote_verbatim: the only way to see if an object or a service or a website, whatever you're designing really works is to build the prototype and show it to people, let them try, observe the people using your prototype and iterate
claims.speaker: Massimo Banzi
claims.episode_title: Arduino's Invisible Touch with Massimo Banzi

attribution_notes: ep135: header speaker was the interviewer; the consulting practice described is the guest's own, so the claim is attributed to Mike Harrison.
ep176: the passage fuses two voices; the production-panel dimensional-tweak claim is left null because the speaker cannot be resolved from content.
